documentTitle: Emergency Access, Contingency Outage & Live Occupancy Integrity

sections.sectionTitle: Minimum 3.5 m Unobstructed Ambulance & Fire Tender Access
sections.summary: Emergency vehicle routes require at least 3.5 m continuous clear width without stalls, stages, barricades, or overhead constrictions.
sections.verbatimQuote: Emergency ambulance and fire access lanes must maintain a minimum continuous clear width of 3.5 meters free of rigid structures, barricades, or parked service equipment.

sections.summary: Test closing any single primary exit or central corridor to ensure no gathering zone becomes isolated and surviving exits retain sufficient egress width.
sections.verbatimQuote: Contingency planning should verify N-1 egress redundancy by testing the closure of any single exit gate or main corridor to ensure surviving backup routes prevent zone isolation.

sections.sectionTitle: External Assembly Points & Authority Command Deference
sections.summary: External assembly points must be situated outside primary egress bottlenecks and all real-world evacuation commands must defer to officially approved response plans and statutory authorities.
sections.verbatimQuote: Planning tools support layout contingency evaluation only; all real-world evacuation declarations, crowd dispersal orders, and emergency command decisions belong strictly to statutory police, fire, medical, and civil authorities.

sections.sectionTitle: Segregated Live Occupancy Channels & Staleness Discipline
sections.summary: Never blend manual headcounts, pass scan telemetry, and practice simulation streams into one combined count; tag every figure with source, timestamp, and staleness warning.
sections.verbatimQuote: Live control-centre occupancy displays must keep manual staff counts, electronic pass-scan totals, and practice drill streams strictly segregated with explicit source labels, timestamps, and staleness indicators.

sections.sectionTitle: Role of Crowd Simulation in Relative Layout Comparison
sections.summary: Deterministic agent simulations illustrate relative differences between layout snapshots under identical random seeds and are never exact predictions of real-world emergency behavior.
sections.verbatimQuote: Planning-stage crowd simulations provide controlled relative comparisons between alternative layouts under fixed assumptions and must never be interpreted as exact predictions of real-world emergency or stampede behavior.
